definition: Disparate means fundamentally different, or made up of sharply contrasting and unrelated parts.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word disparate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know disparate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The planning committee united people with disparate backgrounds, from dairy farmers to software engineers.
Different can describe any two things that are not the same, while disparate suggests elements so unlike that they barely seem to belong together.
Disparate is milder than irreconcilable, which means so deeply opposed that the elements can never be brought into agreement.

Dissimilar is the measured, neutral way to say two things are not alike, and it carries no drama - two dissimilar designs can still sit comfortably side by side. Disparate is stronger: the elements are so fundamentally unlike that they hardly seem to belong in the same collection at all.

Contrasting things are strikingly different in a way that plays them off each other - contrasting colors are often paired on purpose because the difference works. Disparate elements do not set each other off; they simply share no common ground, so putting them together feels arbitrary rather than artful.

Unrelated is about connection: two unrelated events simply have no link between them, and the word passes no judgment on how they look. Disparate is about character: the pieces are jarringly unalike in kind. Two unrelated songs might happen to sound similar; disparate songs could never be mistaken for one family.
